```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 110,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4, out.width = "100%")
library(excalidrawer)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Two ways in

`sketch()` draws any plot in Excalidraw style, at the size of whatever device
it lands on, so it works in the plot pane, in knitr chunks and with `ggsave()`.

```{r, fig.alt = "A hand-drawn stacked bar chart titled Drive train by class, bars filled in pastel Excalidraw colours"}
p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill = drv)) + geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_excalidraw() + labs(title = "Drive train by class", x = NULL)
sketch(p)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ggsave("drive.png", sketch(p), width = 8, height = 5)
```

`as_excalidraw()` returns the scene itself, ready to annotate, restyle, save
or open in Excalidraw:

```{r, fig.alt = "The bar chart as an Excalidraw scene, drawn in hand-drawn style"}
s <- as_excalidraw(p)
s
```

By default plots get `theme_excalidraw()` (handwriting font, ink axes, no
grey panel). Pass `theme = NULL` to keep your own theme. Other options:
`fill_style`, `roughness`, `font`, `outline`, `preset` and `seed`.

```{r, fig.alt = "The bar chart again with cross-hatched fills, extra-sloppy cartoonist lines and the Virgil font"}
as_excalidraw(p, fill_style = "cross-hatch", roughness = "cartoonist", font = "Virgil") |>
  plot()
```

## Annotations with data values

Scenes made from a ggplot remember how data values map to positions, so
annotations can point at the data. Categories map to their centre; wrap a
number in `I()` to give pixels instead.

```{r, fig.alt = "A hand-drawn bar chart of cars by class titled What do people drive?, with a box around the SUV bar, a circle on compact, a sticky note saying SUVs win! with an arrow, and a callout saying only 5 of these by the 2seater bar"}
cars <- ggplot(mpg, aes(class)) + geom_bar(fill = "#a5d8ff") + labs(x = NULL, y = "cars")
as_excalidraw(cars) |>
  exc_title("What do people drive?") |>
  exc_mark(x = "suv", y = c(0, 62), type = "box") |>
  exc_mark(x = "compact", y = 47, type = "circle") |>
  exc_note("SUVs win!", x = "midsize", y = 52, to = c("suv", 50)) |>
  exc_callout("only 5 of these", x = "2seater", y = 5, dx = 30, dy = -70) |>
  plot()
```

`exc_mark()` types: `"circle"`, `"box"`, `"underline"`, `"highlight"`,
`"strike"`, `"bracket"`, `"cross"`.

## Colours

```{r}
excalidraw_colors("stroke", 6)
excalidraw_colors("background", 6)
```

`scale_fill_excalidraw()` uses the light fills and `scale_colour_excalidraw()`
the strong strokes; the `_c` versions run through the shades of one hue.

## Base graphics

```{r, fig.alt = "A hand-drawn histogram of Old Faithful waiting times in minutes, bars filled in light orange"}
sketch(~ hist(faithful$waiting, col = "#ffd8a8", main = "Waiting time", xlab = "minutes"))
```

## Presets

```{r, fig.alt = "A hand-drawn scatter plot of highway mileage against engine size, coloured by drive train, in the blueprint preset: white lines on blue"}
sketch(ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
         scale_colour_excalidraw(), preset = "blueprint")
```
